recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. A future publisher build should regenerate rendered artifacts from the corrected StructureDefinition; if the work group wants identical CID 33 binding-description cleanup on other resources, track that as a separate bounded terminology wording task.
issue_request: FHIR-17279 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5 by Imaging Integration. It asked whether ImagingStudy.modality and ImagingStudy.series.modality should remain acquisition-only CID 29/extensible bindings; the final resolution selected DICOM CID 33 Modality, retained extensible binding strength, removed acquisition-only terminology if unused, and updated the ImagingStudy modality definitions to include acquisition and non-acquisition modalities.
initial_application: The issue was initially applied in e64cab69af, a combined ImagingStudy update commit for GF#17279 and related issues. That commit changed the old ImagingStudy spreadsheet from DICOM CID 29/acquisition-only text to CID 33 and non-acquisition modality wording. Later source refactoring moved the authoritative resource definition into source/imagingstudy/structuredefinition-ImagingStudy.xml.
additional_context: ImagingStudy is an active current-build resource in source/fhir.ini and is assigned to the ii work group. Current source already used the DICOM CID 33 value set and the element definitions already allowed acquisition and non-acquisition modalities. Later FHIR-50775/FHIR-53181 wording updates preserved that interpretation. Community searches found no direct Confluence or Zulip discussion for FHIR-17279; related Zulip terminology discussion supports the DICOM CID 33 external value set use and does not conflict with this cleanup.
reconciliation: Changed the binding.description values for ImagingStudy.modality and ImagingStudy.series.modality from "Type of acquired data in the instance." to "DICOM Modality values, including acquisition and non-acquisition modalities." No binding strength, value set URL, cardinality, or element definition changed.
